errors.evidence: The description only covers the line for the Eurozone and partially for Belgium. It omits the description for the other six lines present in the chart: Griechenland, Deutschland, Spanien, Frankreich, Irland, and Italien.
The last sentence is truncated and incomplete. It ends abruptly with the number '10', while the full sentence should have probably stated a value around '108 %'.
The line for the Eurozone ('Eurozone') starts in 1995 at a value that is visibly higher than 70%, approximately at 73%.
In the description of the line for Belgium ('Belgien'), the value for the year 2014 is stated as 'rund 105 %', but the chart shows it at approximately 107%.
